title: TAP OAuth Client Secret
description: Schema for an OAuth 2.0 client-credential secret consumed by a tap_auth provider (req-tap-auth-providers / req-tap-auth-google-oidc / req-tap-auth-github-oauth). Both provider types TAP ships hold the SAME two fields — an OIDC client credential IS an OAuth 2.0 client credential — so there is one schema and one resolver, and the kind names which protocol issued it rather than forking the shape. The file reuses the established tap-cares '*.secret.json' envelope (scope/key/kind/description/data — spec-tap-cares-secrets), which tap-cares validates structurally; tap_auth owns this kind-specific schema for the 'oidc_client' data block (client_id/client_secret) since tap-cares deliberately does not validate kind-specific data. The secret is bind-mounted under TAP_SECRETS_ROOT, gitignored ('*.secret.json'), and resolved by scope:key through the tap-cares secret registry — never embedded in a boot profile or DB row. A provider config references this secret by its key; resolve_secrets() validates the loaded data against this schema in the provider's offline self-test.

scope.description: tap-cares secret registry scope. Fixed to 'auth' for tap_auth provider secrets so they are namespaced apart from collector secrets.

key.description: Local key within the 'auth' scope. MUST equal the file basename (<key>.secret.json) AND the provider 'id' that references this secret (e.g. 'example-google'). Stable natural key, lowercase with hyphens.

kind.description: Consumer-defined secret kind. 'oidc_client' for an OIDC client credential (google_oidc); 'oauth2_client' for a plain OAuth 2.0 one (github_oauth — GitHub publishes no OpenID discovery document for user login, so calling its credential an OIDC client would be a false label). Either selects this schema for the 'data' block; the two carry identical fields.

description.description: Free-form operator note: what this secret is, which provider/IdP it belongs to, and why it exists (mandatory — every secret explains itself).

data.description: The OAuth 2.0 client credentials issued by the IdP (for Google: Google Cloud Console > Credentials > OAuth 2.0 Client ID, type 'Web application'; for GitHub: Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps > New OAuth App). Secret material — never logged in full; the client_secret is redacted in all logs.

client_id.description: OAuth 2.0 client identifier (Google: '...apps.googleusercontent.com'; GitHub: an 'Ov23li...'/'Iv1....'-style Client ID). Not itself secret, but stored alongside the secret for atomic provisioning.

client_secret.description: OAuth 2.0 client secret (Google: 'GOCSPX-...'; GitHub: the generated client secret, shown once at creation). Highly sensitive; resolved into allauth settings in memory only, never persisted to a DB row or boot profile and redacted in logs.

metadata.description: Optional non-secret operator metadata for diagnostics (e.g. GCP project id, rotation date). Never secret material.
